A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pruning All-Rounder (PAR) work. All ten pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original PAR evaluations on LLaVA and Qwen-VL, component ablations in Tables 1-3, and redundancy analyses and qualitative examples in Figures 2, 4, and 5.

after.justification: V2 retains original PAR benchmark results, component ablations, redundancy analyses, and a qualitative pruning example in Tables 1-3 and Figures 2 and 4.

M1.justification: The transformer meta-router, layer-controller embeddings, Gaussian-noise preference construction, KL-based comparison, reference-free preference objective, and token/layer selection procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.2 adds clarification about preserving visual features and alignment; revised pruning budgets concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions use LLaVA-80k preference data and the same eight named benchmarks in Section 5.1 and Table 1. Although v2 claims nine benchmarks elsewhere, it identifies and reports no ninth benchmark or additional task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds gamma-MoD, which was only cited in v1, and removes TokenPacker, M3, PruMerge, and the retrained LLaVolta comparison. V2's retained LLaVolta rows match v1's '(test)' rows. FastV, ShortGPT, random dropping, and RoE-LLaVA remain. This substantially changes the main comparator set.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1-5.2 change the stated training pruning budget from K=4, M=432 to K=4, M=400. Reported token budgets also change within retained experiments, including Table 3's token and joint ablations from T=144 to T=176. These are revisions within the existing evaluation design; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 removes Figure 5's baseball case study comparing attention maps, noise perturbation, selected tokens, and resulting answers. The preliminary redundancy analyses, component-ablation questions, and fire-hydrant pruning example remain, with revised budgets and cost annotations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five noise seeds in Section 3.3 and retain Figure 2's boxplots and error bars. Neither introduces additional repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: Efficiency results change throughout Tables 1-3 and Figure 4: LLaVA FastV changes from 5.78 to 5.93 TFLOPs, and full Qwen-VL from 9.27 to 10.01. Full LLaVA's MME score changes from 1467 to 1510. Several comparator/configuration results and all averages disappear, while gamma-MoD results are added. Most retained task scores remain identical, sometimes under revised conditions: PAR's POPE 76.1 and SEED 62.7 move from T=144/L=28 to T=176/L=28. These do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4 retain the same generation formulation, router mapping, action scoring, and optimization objective. No formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction expands claimed validation coverage from eight to nine benchmarks, although the documented experiments remain at eight. The principal claims about joint self-supervised pruning, frozen LVLM weights, and flexible pruning configurations remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly emphasizes that the router learns pruning decisions without changing visual features or realigning vision and language. V2 removes the Figure 5 interpretation that noise redirects attention toward the baseball bat and swinging arm. The central token-layer correlation interpretation remains.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a repository link and states that code is publicly available, replacing v1's future-release promise. Conversely, Table 2 drops explicit T=72 and L=24 annotations for specialized pruning configurations. Hardware, batch size, sample count, and stated training time remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work gains separate parameter- and token-pruning discussions, a task-specific/task-agnostic classification, and expanded coverage of VTW, HiRED, and Fit-Prune. The introduction explicitly credits ShortGPT's layer-redundancy study and visual contrastive decoding as inspiration. Several references are added or removed, while the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and introduction, expands and splits the compression-related-work subsection, clarifies optimization prose, and shortens the qualitative discussion and conclusion. Affiliations change and acknowledgments are added. The main section sequence and most method exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 replaces separate retrained/frozen panels, averages, and colored FastV-relative annotations with a unified, FLOP-oriented comparison using boldface highlights. Figure 5 is removed, Figure 3 and Table 3 move, and Figure 1 is restyled. These substantially revise the central visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution, clarifies frozen-backbone optimization, reports code availability, and makes some FLOP percentages more internally consistent. However, it removes comparator and attention-map evidence, drops Table 1's retrained/frozen distinction, and claims nine benchmarks while documenting eight. Substantial token-budget and FLOP revisions accompany largely unchanged scores without explaining whether these are corrections or changed experiments. Their effect on the central efficiency evidence remains unclear, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
